newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Third mining company interested in Konkola copper.
newsitem.headline: Third mining company interested in Konkola copper.

text.p: Zambia Copper Investments Ltd said on Thursday another international mining house was interested in the Zambian Konkola Deep copper project following the withdrawal earlier this year of WMC Ltd.
Bermuda-based ZCI is a unit of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's.

Anglo agreed with the Zambian government at the start of the year to undertake to form a consortium of investors to develop the Konkola Deep Mining Mining Project, in conjunction with state-run Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd.
Gencor Ltd is also participating in the consortium but Australia's WMC withdrew after intially participating.
"Another international mining company has expressed interest in the project and its decision on whether to participate in the consortium is awaited," ZCI said in a statement.

The Zambian government and Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) recently accepted the recommendations of British merchant bank NM Rothschild on the privatisation of the copper giant. The Zambia Privatisation Agency last week invited pre-qualification bids for ZCCM assets.

The disposal of ZCCM assets -- including the Konkola project -- is expected to be completed in the second half of 1997 with the government then disposing of all or a substantial part of its shareholding in ZCCM in the first half of 1998.
Developing the 350 million tonnes Konkola Deep project is seen as crucial to the future of Zambia's copper mining industry.

ZCI said negotiations on the financial, legal and technical issues of developing Konkola -- including the assets that will form part of the package -- were continuing with the government and ZCCM with a view to concluding a memorandum of understanding (MOU).
After that there will be a detailed feasibility study.

"Subject to a satisfactory outcome to the negotiations on the MOU and the finalisation of a bankable feasibility study indicating an aceptable return, both sides are committed to the implementation of the project at the earliest possible date," ZCI said.
Zambia produced around 380,000 tonnes of copper last year, making it the world's seventh largest producer. The government said in June it expected copper output to treble following privatisation.
Anglo is a minority shareholder in state-run ZCCM, holding 27.3 percent via ZCI.
